July 23 (UPI) -- The European Commission on Thursday fined Google more than $1 billion for violating the Digital Markets Act in its use of gate-keeping in its search engine and on Google Play.

The Commission found that Google favors its own products in search results, suggesting tools like shopping, hotels, transportation and sports results over those of third parties. It also accused Google of not allowing app developers to communicate with customers or allow them to inform customers of alternative, often cheaper, offers and to direct them to those offers to make purchases, for example on websites or alternative app stores. It also displayed its own products higher up in Google Play searches than competitors.

"The best products should succeed because they're better, not because they're owned by the company running the search engine," Teresa Ribera, the executive vice president of the European Commission overseeing competition policy, said in a statement Thursday. "This is the promise of the DMA, protecting fairness, choice and innovation in digital markets for the benefit of all European citizens."

The Commission said Google has 60 days to comply with the DMA or face further fines of up to 5% of its global revenue.

Kent Walker, Google's general counsel, told The New York Times that the product changes the Commission is requiring would harm services for EU users.

"This isn't fair competition; it's product degradation," Walker said. "Regulation should improve products, not make them worse."

How President Donald Trump will respond to this fine is something Brussels is watching. Previously, Trump has threatened heavy tariffs on countries that he believes are unfairly targeting American tech companies or those that charge digital services taxes. He's expected to announce new EU tariffs Friday.

Google has been fined billions by the European Commission in recent years.

It slapped Google with a $4.9 billion fine in 2018, saying its pre-installation deals with smartphone makers abused Android's mobile dominance. In 2022, a court reduced the fine to $4.67 billion.

Last year, the Commission fined Google $3.73 billion for anti-competitive practices in its advertising technology business.

On Wednesday, Google parent company Alphabet reported $112.1 billion in quarterly profits, The Times reported.
